item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) A Young Reality Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid male that would accidentally warp-reality if he has too much stress or gets intensely outrageous.

Central Narrative:
SCP-XXXX is a reality-altering humanoid male that is approximately 2 feet tall. The subject will accidentally disrupt reality if mental capacities are largely due to it being the source that can affect their power's capabilities, efficacy, and limitations.

SCP-XXXX was discovered when reports of a paranormal event have occurred, which is shown to be various vehicles falling from the skies. After this was brought to the Foundation, they've located all of the scene witnesses and wipe out their memories. Before doing so, they've asked the witnesses whether they know the cause of the phenomena. The civilians all said that they have no clue what the cause could be. The agents all know that who, or whatever could do so, is somewhere around in that area, as they've asked each people in the area until they've move to the house of a high school male, which eventually claims that he is the caused of the phenomenon. After this, the Foundation has ordered the agents to lied to the boy's parents that he's going to school abroad.

In the interview, SCP-XXXX stated that he discovered his abilities when his father forces him to do a lot of work, which causes him a big amount of stress, also causes him to have a few mental stabilities problem1.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The high-school is a person who lives in a family with a very rigorous father. Due to seeing his son being too joyful and doesn't seem to care whether if he gets in trouble, the father always scolds him non-stop, slowly affecting his mental health.

Additional Notes:

Footnotes
1. Stated that he sometimes talks alone, play with his pencil, walks, run, and jumps around in circles while pulling his hair and talking alone at the same time.

item.title: Aerosol SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking green light: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Page layout: Standard SCP format with several addendums and a link to an offset page.

Elevator pitch: The SCP is an anomalous aerosol created by the Manna Charitable Foundation with the intention of reducing the Earth's temperature to halt or reduce global warming by reflecting the Sun's rays using anomalously enhanced sulfur dioxide which are designed to last longer and grow even larger by abosrbing Co2 in the atmosphere. The conprocs for the first iteration states that its currently uncontained and personal assigned are to work on either containing it or lessen its negative effects, as well as preventing the public from learning its anomalous effects.

In the second iteration, the conprocs states its the cause of an active GK-Class "Ozone destruction" scenario and while they are working on to stop by spreading alkaline all across the atmosphere, their unsure if it'll work or not due to the magnitude of the SCP.

Central narrative: A long time ago, the MCF was working on Project Sunna to try and fix global warming as its directly/indirectly responsible for a lot of bad things happening in the world, with funding from not only some governments but also anomaloud GoIs. Its the biggest project MCF has created.

They then released it via planes into the atmosphere which worked for a while; however, as years gone by, the ozone became severely damaged in some parts of the world to the point where thousands are dying. As the SCP Foundation is trying to stop it, the MCF however have fallen and received a shit ton of backlash for this.

Hook: While it maybe another one of those MCF articles where they try to do good things, only to end in disaster this one however takes it to another, global scale where the MCF really fucked up.

Notes: I need someone to help fact check these things to make sure if at least some of it correct.

item.title: "Man of None"
item.description: Anyone who acknowledges a relationship between the man and themselves dies painfully within 24 hours.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror / Drama / Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): It'll begin as a standardized SCP document, listing the object class, containment procedures, etc etc. The bulk of the article, however, will be inside of the addendum - the interviews, more specifically.

Elevator Pitch: A man under the affect of a seeming "curse". Anyone who verbally confirms any relationship between them and the man dies within the next 24 hours in an unspeakably horrific way, varying from person to person.

Central Narrative: Man of None", a concept I had for an SCP, is a seemingly regular man with a personal love for technology. However, what is strange is the fact anyone who verbally recognizes a relationship between the speaker and the object are killed within 24 hours in an unspeakably painful way. While this may seem as if it's simply for the shock factor of gore and horrific deaths, there's a much darker thing behind it.
He wants to die, however due to the nature of the SCP Foundation his death would be something which would not be wanted. So, they contain him and give him psychological treatment (of course on a very strict regiment), however it never helps. With plenty of research, the only way which suicide patients are helped is via forming relationships with those who help them. And, any relationship with him causes horrific death. So, he's left alone in the world. All that people will call him is an object. They will not say he's their "friend". Not a "loved one". "Family", "enemy", any of the sort is never heard from them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man, due to irrelevant trauma, has developed [REDACTED] disorder - which, with hints throughout the article, would be Borderline Personality Disorder. He is absolutely desperate for some form of recognition, approval, or relationship between another human. However, due to the nature of his "curse", he's unable to. This plays to one of the largest human fears of being truly alone. He goes through phases of being desperate for someone to tell him that they care for him in some form, and phases of attempting to hide from others so they don't die a horrific death. He's seen numerous of the things which he's caused, which leaves a permanent trauma to him.

Additional Notes: I'm horrific when it comes to formatting first of all, so if I've messed this up please tell me. I'd like criticism on the entire thing really.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.description: A doll wants you to worship it, a little at a time.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Doll of a non-descript female anime figure
  • Causes those nearby to into a near-worship state
  • Demands paltry tribute to stay sated
  • The character is unable to be described, named, nor the anime she is from
  • Individuals under the effect feel compelled to talk about her, discussing objective traits like beauty, coolness, etc.
  • When asked, individuals under the effect will reflect questions such as 'YOU don't know HER?' 'I can't believe you'd have to ask me that; a REAL fan would know.'
  • The doll manifested due to a natural proclivity for 'otaku' obsession.
  • The doll represents a void of concept, it can never be fully filled as an idea, so it seeks material items to sate itself.
  • The student discovered the figure and gradually became a classic case of neglecting himself in favor of the idol, pushing people away while lording over them how great his new obsession was.

Central Narrative:

The doll exists in such a way that it compels those nearby to give it small tokens, with no discernable pattern as to what that item needs to be. It prefers to be above eye level on a shelf. The doll was found in a college dorm closet whose occupant began failing out due to offering term papers and other collegiate supplies. Initially thinking that the student was a hoarder, not much thought was given to the situation until the closet was forcefully cleaned and the student's roommate was found bound, malnourished, and near-death within the mass, assumed to be given as tribute when the student did not have anything else to give.

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days. However, a note from Foundation management has requested that office supplies no longer be offered due to the supply closet constantly needing to be restocked. The longer the doll goes without tribute, the stronger its pull.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The doll possesses both memetic and antimemetic properties, compelling those under its effect to want to talk about her all the time but unable to physically describe any aspect that would give her characterization.

item.title: A genetics enhancement lab
item.description: Glass cage that pushes an individual a few hundred generations forward.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Creepy
Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article, but the plot advances in dialogs between researchers.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is just a glass cage. When you put a specimen inside it, it "reverts" to a single-celled egg, allowing for genetic modification. It will then grow back to the same specimen, but hundreds of generations later, accounting for the modifications brought to it (or not, if there wasn't any).

Central Narrative: The story is based around a doctor and her researcher who tries to understand the SCP, but more importantly what the previous owner was trying to do with it, and what happened to him.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP revolves around damaged notes from the previous owner, describing a few of his experiments, and his downfall. Of course, most of the notes are missing.

Additional Notes: I have written a rough sandbox of it because it's been on my mind for a while, even though it is far from finished. I come back to it and bring changes to it a lot, if you'd like to read it.

item.title: The Mother
item.description: (260 Words) A line of anomalous women all related, when one gives birth, it dies.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) : SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch:
A single branch of anomalous female humanoid creatures dating back to 150 AD. The creature she births brings a new anomalous effect. This effect is non-voluntary, and takes place whenever a criteria is met. This SCP grows at a rate similar to a human being, but once reaching the year of 29, regardless of contact with any males or injections, she will begin to experience the stages of child birth at a rapid pace, giving birth 3 hours later, and self-terminating. Each generation is only female, and contains one or more anomalous power.

Central Narrative:
A linear narrative; The capture of the SCP, attempts to contain each generation, attempts to try to stop the birth process, attempted force abortions, subsequent failures, attemps at containing the 'reincarnations' of this SCP as they come, and the learning of how this SCP functions on a deeper level.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Each female born from this line carries one or more strong anomalous powers, such as the ability to create and snuff out fires, the ability to warp reality, or the ability to instantly terminate any creature that is in it's area when angry. The seemingly randomness of anomalous power after birth leaving to a constant struggle in contain each generation, and changing of the classification of the SCP. This SCP is only one familial line, not expanding out towards other families.

Additional Notes:
Article will contain multiple tabs that each have their own interviews, tests, and trials done on the SCP, leaving it open for infinite possibilities. I do not know how to do this yet, but would like some ideas on where to look to do this.

item.title: SCP *PLACE HOLDER NUMBER* The Bee movie.
item.description: This is my very first draft of an SCP, I want to know what y'all think of it.
item.content:encoded:
For context before we get into the meat of this thread, I was inspired to write this because I've often heard the bee movie be described as a collective fever dream, I feel like it could fit into the joke scp category, but I think with more tweaking it could be a full fledged article.

Scp 9999 The Bee movie.

Object class: Safe.

Special containment procedures:

Due to the circumstances surrounding SCP 9999 full scale containment as of this moment is both impossible and unnecessary. Personnel are instead instructed to avoid viewing SCP 9999, MTF-PHI 22 “Fever Dreamers” is to be alerted to any devices reported to contain a recording of SCP 9999, recordings are to be either destroyed or given directly to Director McKinley for [DATAEXPUNGED]. If any personnel should happen to view SCP 9999 they are instructed to avoid telling others about it or posting about it on social media in order to attempt to slow the spread of its anomalous effects.

Description:

SCP 9999 is the official designation for a viral phenomenon which causes the victim to hallucinate having viewed a computer animated movie from 2007 called The Bee Movie which stars comedian Jerry Seinfeld. Those affected usually have wildly different experiences in regards to SCP 9999, with some reporting that the film they watched was a romantic comedy, while others report that the film they watched was a surreal horror film, in spite of this however four factors remain constant.

Number one: the main character is always voiced by Jerry Seinfeld.

Number two: the main character will attempt to sue the human race over their consumption of honey.

Number three: the love interest of the main character will always be human.

Number four: the film will always end with The main character and the love interest opening a joined flower shop/law firm.

Although the foundation has managed to create a ‘dummy film’ and amnestise most of those who have been affected by SCP 9999, there remain a few affected individuals who further propagate the effects of SCP 9999.

item.title: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.description: It's a chemically changing rock.
item.content:encoded:
It's a chemically changing rock. Name is work in progress, and I'm not too happy with the discovery, so any help/suggestions would be nice

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/intriguing?

Page Layout (Optional): Standard article. After description, will go over discovery, and after discovery will then go over test logs.

Elevator Pitch: It's a tall rock that slightly twists. The tip of it will be called element A, and the base of it will be called element B. If an object touches the tip, element A changes into the majority of the atoms in that object. There are various things that cause a teleport event, but when that happens, the spire disappears and reappears at a random spot on the earth. element B then becomes the old element A, element A becomes the closest solid element near the tip, and the spire absorbs every current element B atom in a 1km radius.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It was discovered when a redacted reality bender started rampaging, and along with various other items it created the spire. Some clean up MTF member accidentally touches the tip with his glove, and his glove disappears along with the spire. It's found in some town where around half of the people there dropped dead and withered on the spot, because the glove was mostly carbon, and all the carbon was stolen from their bodies. The spire is found in the town, and it's got a carbon base with a solid oxygen tip (from the oxygen in the granite that built the town)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The rules for the spire are pretty strict, so it's like a constant reminder that whatever the old tip was, all those atoms could immediately disappear in the center of a city, but it could also appear in the center of a forest, and be difficult to track down, so I feel that would draw people into the story. Also there's a mention near the beginning about testing being discontinued, so I feel people would want to see why

Additional Notes: The things that cause a teleportation event(work in progress name) are: The tip is touched with the same majority atom as the tip already had, so instead of staying the same it teleports. 108 hours pass without a tip change. If the tip is a radioactive element, the moment an atom in it decays, it undergoes the event (which is pretty much instantly). If the tip and base are the same element, it undergoes the event. If the tip is helium, it undergoes the event. I can explain more, as a lot of the info had to be cut down due to size limit.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA - Greenlights needed!
item.description: A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind-
item.content:encoded:
A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind- find themselves adapting to the modern climate in order to seek their prey.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Comedy, mainly, but not in an un-serious manner.

Elevator Pitch: You know those clearly fake ads you get on nsfw websites? The ones that’re like “HOT SINGLES IN YOUR AREA”, et cetera. Yeah. Those, but anomalous, and set up by Sirens, as in the type that’d lure sailors to death. The ad, if loaded on a page, would display a message along the lines of “10 HOT (xyz) WITHIN (distance)! TEXT NOW!”

+ show block
– hide block

As time went by, the distance would gradually decrease, and the number increase. This would culminate in the subject being ambushed, and then… well, consumed, by a number of horrible, vaguely humanoid fishy-people.

The Foundation would later track these ads to a certain location, and, unable to block the ads via webcrawlers or other non-anomalous means, would send in an MTF team to find out what’s going on. There’s an exploration log, and the anomaly is accidentally neutralised when the coven of sirens panics upon realising there’s angry fellows with guns in the hideout and collapses the building in order to escape, breaking all of their paratech that let them make and maintain the anomalous ads in the first place.

Central Narrative: The context behind this strange new manner of Greek monsters luring in prey is simply that people don’t usually fall for the ole’ “Sing to the sailors until they follow you and drown” trick, and they’ve had to resort to new and unusual means of tracking targets. Inkeeping with the tradition of luring sailors in with beautiful songs and false faces, they decide to essentially hijack NSFW spam ads, which ends up working pretty well.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I’m aware, nobody’s done sirens as an SCP before, and beyond that, the concept of the fake ads on the sides of sketchy sites actually being dangerous beyond just giving your computer malware is a little spine-chilling. And also really funny, when you think about it.

Additional Notes: As this would be my first SCP, essentially any critique at all would be greatly appreciated.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.description: A tale about SCP-1498.
item.content:encoded:
A troublesome teenager utilizes mysterious livestock to control his dreams. A tale about SCP-1498.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: Tale

This tale doesn't take place in The Foundation itself. It's based around one specific SCP before it was contained.

Elevator Pitch: A teenager by the name of Ty encounters SCP-1498 in the woods, and begins to abuse its abilities. However, when he slowly starts to become an instance of SCP-1498, he struggles to find help. This takes place a month before SCP-1498's original containment date.

Central Narrative: Taking place in august of 1965, just before SCP-1498 (which this tale is about) is contained, a troublesome teenager, Ty, stumbles across SCP-1498 in the woods and learns that he can order dreams from the SCP. He begins to abuse the ability, spending most of his time asleep, dreaming. However, when his body begins to slowly turn into instances of the SCP, he attempts to find "The Oneiroi Collective" (the people who possibly designed the SCP) to help him. However, upon searching phone books, he discovers that the phone number to call them only exists on the instances of SCP-1498. He hurries back to where he last saw them, but they've vanished completely. Luckily, a phone wire that goes through the woods leads him to an abandoned office building, where he finds the livestock entering. Ty catches up to them, managing to get on the phone with The Oneiroi Collective. However, it's too late, and Ty completely transforms into an instance of SCP-1498-1, mindlessly wandering back into the woods, ironically dreaming of the days when he didn't dream at all.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The realization that Ty basically has no way out of the situation he's in. This is the foundation of most of the tension throughout the tale, as it will seem almost completely hopeless. Which, by the end, it's revealed that it was, indeed, hopeless. At least, that's the goal I'll try to achieve with this tale.

Additional Notes: Obviously, this is a rough outline of what happens, and it will almost certainly change (hopefully for the better) if this gets greenlighted. I'm also not the author of SCP-1498, and as so tried to keep this story as distant from the lore set up in the SCP itself.

Here's a link to SCP-1498, which this tale is based on: http://www.scpwiki.com/scp-1498

Central Narrative: The armor was discovered during the Vietnam war and captured by the Foundation they then found through testing and a few containment incidents the basic abilities of the armor as well as learning with untrained individuals it will cause them to enter a blood rage upon putting it on and it will deteriorate their body killing them within hours of exposure. The armor also has access to famous warrior throughout history and the deterioration seen in subjects is most likely due to this effect as the armor will steal and contain your spirit. It also has a calling effect that pulls nearby personnel into attempting to wear it resulting in their deaths. The armor was originally created during the Battle of Thermopylae when a Persian soldier donned the armor of Leonidas causing his spirit to put a curse on the armor (causing the effects seen today).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP is a tool the Foundation can use to combat many of the threats the Foundation faces however it is a very unstable tool and finding a suitable subject is incredibly difficult as most will die within hours, also it creates an effect similar to the "One Ring" from Lord of the Rings in which it pulls people towards it and typically has them fight over the owner of the armor which is very dangerous as many valuable Foundation assets could be drawn to it and die to the wearer. Also the amount of knowledge the armor holds from its past users could prove useful to the Foundation as well as its extensive knowledge of strategy.

Additional Notes: I feel as if I am missing something to make this story truly unique and I hope someone can take notes on this and help me figure out how to properly narrow down my ideas or give it an extra hook of some sort.

item.title: Memetic Instruction Pamphlets
item.description: Anomalous instruction pamphlets designed to maim/kill
item.content:encoded:
Anomalous instruction pamphlets designed to maim/kill seemingly random people across the globe… (all criticism welcome)

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous set of pamphlets that compel the reader to do whatever the pamphlet has written on it- for example, if one said "read this pamphlet over and over", the subject would be forced to read the pamphlet over and over until it is taken from them or they expire.

Central Narrative: A group of researchers testing the capabilities of the SCP after MTF recovery units with memetic resistance find multiple pamphlets in seemingly random homes in urban areas such as Berlin, NYC, and London. Interviews with the owners of the homes show that they all have had attempts on their lives through anomalous means within the past three months.

+ show block
– hide block

The people are administered amnestics and are put back in their homes with a Foundation agent trailing them to make sure they are not killed. The researchers begin investigations on possible reasons why the makers of the pamphlets are targeting these people. One of the D-Class testing personnel notices that the contents of the pamphlet have changed.

The pamphlet writes about how the hitmen attempting to kill these people know that the Foundation has acquired the pamphlets and that the hitmen will not be so careless in the future, potentially setting up an opportunity for there to be more to the story.

The Foundation intercepts a radio transmission detailing the failure of the pamphlets, and discussing potential plans for the future. Foundation agents find a connection between the targets of the killings: they have all been involved in numerous black-market purchases of anomalous objects.

The Foundation discovers the existence of a group of assassins hired by existing groups to carry out their dirty work. The group has been implicated in over 260 murders, burglaries and other crimes across the globe, starting in 2008.

The article ends with all the pamphlets changing to contain the message WE’LL BE WATCHING. SIGNED WITH LOVE, THE SWORD OF THE KING

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The different pamphlets have different instructions tailored to the individuals who received them. Each of them seems to be designed to seriously maim or kill the person who received them. The mystery of why these people are being targeted by anomalous killers is also a good hook.

Additional Notes: With this SCP, I am hoping to set up an opportunity for a new GOI or POI and more SCPs. All criticism is appreciated!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Central Narrative: The facility has found out that the human species as they know it is evolving with the newest generation being able to manipulate the code of any piece of technology using their mind and captured the first kid to show these signs(commonly known as "The First" among the other Evolves) and has been testing on him and others that were found next for the reasons of the evolution and the part of the brain being affected by the evolution.

After the incident that happened with The First where he hacked into the foundation's database, the foundation has made a firewall to keep these evolves out of their system and later redirect their signals to a simulation of their database with them thinking that they are hacking into the actual database while they can reverse engineer on their signals.

The scientists soon find out that the signal structure of the signals produced by The First is different from other Evolves and start later focus all the research on him to find out what makes him different. On later research that his mind is capable of engineering a virus when he is provided with a high grade computer and some other materials. The virus created attacks on the human brain and shuts it down in 2-3 days. When an infected is in contact with any computer, the virus will inject some of its code which will act as a computer virus capable of taking down the entire NASA Database in a single day.

The scientists are currently reverse engineering on the virus while examining the procedure through which it was made.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The foundation is corrupted and is looking forward to turning the virus into a weapon for their own usage. A scientist has found out about this and carefully hid a message in the article in the hope that someday a person would find the message and do the right thing. The message would be found by deciphering a number suspiciously occurring in the article again and again. Difficulty of deciphering the number would be easy.

item.title: Te Horoi Pai (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Second SCP proposal based on a revisited concept.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Mystery

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: A tube of Petroleum jelly. When ointment is applied to a human, a person's hygiene is enhanced. Prominent symptom manifest in the form of pheromone secretion and irrational compulsion to spread the ointment. Hours after patient zero is infected, the infected encounter amorphous entities. Appearing entities embody subconscious fetishes or extremest fears. They ignore beings lacking pheromone and are hostile to those marked with pheromone.

Central Narrative: On the 9th December, the mysterious disappearance of 25 guests and staff at the Westhaven Luxury Lodge made national headlines. A team of four Field Agents stationed at Nelson, New Zealand take over the investigation and create a cover story.

Field Agents are briefed about the crime scene by the police. Exploring the lodge they find five rooms in the hallway cordoned off by police tape. Foundation agents are alarmed by the crude messages scratched into the Manuka wood and signs glued onto the walls left behind by the lodging's former occupants. Text advertise and revere "a conditioner sent by the gods". Most jarringly, the other remainder of the text read "The knavish resistance were enlightened, now they too relish the heaven-sent scent". Conditioner called "Te Horoi Pai" , translated to Xtreme Conditioner is discovered and placed in containment. All other copies found in the Lodging or within Police custody are confiscated and destroyed.

Testing is conducted, discovering the anomaly's psycho-contagious nature. It's speculated an unknown G.O.I is at hand. A nationwide sweep, extensively covering every hotel, motel and supermarket in New Zealand, yields negative results. A Mobile Taskforce (Called Bad Hair Day) is conceived to monitor the domestic supply chain for wild instances.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Mass disappearance is unheard-of in the 21st century, creating mystery. The anomaly takes place in New Zealand. Testing reveals the ultimate fate of the Lodging's residents. Furthermore, the G.O.I theory is a hypothesis, since Te Horoi Pai is the product name but there is no brand associated nor a manufacturer stated on the bottle. Therefore, the Foundation attempts to contain a contagious SCP with no identified point of origin; an analogy for viral outbreak clusters with no immediate causes.

Additional Notes: This is a submission for my first "canon" SCP, so any form of criticism is appreciated (Bluntness is 100% tolerated but please be constructive).

item.title: IMAGINE YOU WERE THERE: Potential SCP
item.description: A sadistic man tells stories of violence; people who listen to the end suffer the fate of the characters
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, Discovery, Incident Reports, Interview

Elevator Pitch: A sadistic man tells stories of violence and death. People who listen are entranced. However, as the story goes on, listeners start to show signs of physical trauma. When the man finishes his story, any wounds inflicted on the characters in the story appear on the listener, often killing them.

Central Narrative:

The concept is introduced in the Containment Procedures and Description. The SCP is relatively easy to contain, except that his anomalous abilities increase over time unless he is given a D-class to tell a story to. If he is not sated within 8 days, his anomalous abilities begin to work over video, radio, and recordings. If he cannot tell anyone a story in 15 days, he will begin to project mental images of torture and killing into the minds of people outside his containment. After 21 days, this starts to cause minor but real physical damage to those affected. After 28 days, he mentally projects his image of agony onto everyone within several kilometers, which kills most of those affected.

The SCP was discovered and contained after a series of anomalous murders in Tokyo. The SCP seems to understand more about its powers than the Foundation does, and has caused a number of incidents and containment breaches.

In an interview, the SCP recounts its childhood psychopathy, its path to becoming a serial killer, and how it attained its anomalous abilities.

item.title: A problem with alot of scp articles.
item.content:encoded:
Input: 1 chimp (setting: Fine)

Output: [DATA EXPUNGED]

Input: 1 chimp (setting: Rough)

Output: Badly mutilated corpse, showing signs of crushing and cutting with high heat

Those are lines from SCP-914. Why would the SCP use 'chimp' instead of chimpanzee?
A lot of SCPs are structured like poorly-written wikipedia articles, instead of actual scientific reports.
Censored information makes no sense either, why would it be censored in the first place?
Honestly, draft-reviewers should be more informed of things like this.

item.title: Pep-Talk Sticky Notes
item.description: Sticky notes that, when you take one, calm you down.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator Pitch: A sticky note pad that is only useable by personnel currently experiencing negative emotions. When said personnel take one, the message on the note viewable only to them calms them down and leaves them feeling content for a period of three minutes afterward. When the three minutes are up, the subject is left in a neutral state. The messages are reported as upbeat and encouraging.

Central Narrative: It logs how the anomaly is used during testing and ends with a log in which the notepad manifests a secondary anomalous property. It also logs the potential uses of the notepad.

Hook/Attention Grabber I plan the Containment Procedures to be attention-grabbing, with them going something like As SCP-XXXX poses no threat to the security and safety of Site-XX and its personnel, SCP-XXXX is allowed to be freely used whenever it manifests contained in a lock-protected drawer in Dr. XXXXX's office. Also, I plan to put an interview log in which the notepad manifests in the middle of a stressful interview and then manifests to the interviewee after failing the interview miserably.

Additional Notes: I know it's another item SCP, but they work best for my writing style. Also, I want to write this one to be easy to understand for people who have never read an SCP before.

All criticism is appreciated! Thanks!

item.title: EVER EVASIVE BUBBLE!!! IN NEED OF GREENLIGHT!!!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: scp article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: This scp is a bubble with a folded note inside of it. the outside of the note is a face that looks like it is sleeping. the scp seeming to subconsciously avoid all forms of touching. Inside of the folded note may be a memetic symbol, a ground breaking discovery, or a piece of information so horrible, it could shatter even the most sturdy minds.

Central Narrative: This scp was found in a circus that came to [REDACTED] Wisconsin one in a while. A researcher was taking his kids to that circus one day and there was a sign that read ,"EVER-ELUSIVE BUBBLE!!! COME TRY TO POP IT!" the researcher, thinking it would be a great first circus game for them to try, took them into the tent. The kids jumped at the bubble, trying to pop it, and each time, the bubble unnaturally evaded the attempt. The research had called his site director and told him about it. Later after the circus closed, an MTF squad circled the perimeter and closed the circus down. The reason they told the local police and the circus members was because of "safety" and "Drug use". The circus is now a private site of the foundation. several cameras and MTF members have been placed around the perimeter. A monitor room has been placed just outside of the site to keep track of the property.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The note inside of the bubble could have anything in it.
